findings.title: Checksum-only packets now use short BD and lose checksum offload
findings.explanation: This change removes RTE_MBUF_F_TX_TCP_CKSUM, RTE_MBUF_F_TX_UDP_CKSUM and RTE_MBUF_F_TX_IP_CKSUM from the flags that make bnxt_xmit_need_long_bd() return true. A packet that only asks for L3/L4 checksum offload (no TSO, VLAN or tunnel, with TruFlow off) will now go out as a short TX BD. In bnxt_start_xmit, the checksum lflags (TX_BD_LONG_LFLAGS_IP_CHKSUM / TCP_UDP_CHKSUM) are only written to the tx_bd_long_hi descriptor in the long-BD branch. A short BD has nowhere to carry them. The NIC then never computes the checksums, and the packets go on the wire with whatever checksum the application left in the header, which is usually a zero or pseudo-header value. Receivers drop these packets. This hits a very common path, since most apps use checksum offload without TSO. The diff changes only this function (+1/-2), so nothing in the xmit path was updated to handle checksum on the short BD.
findings.suggestion: Put RTE_MBUF_F_TX_TCP_CKSUM, RTE_MBUF_F_TX_UDP_CKSUM and RTE_MBUF_F_TX_IP_CKSUM back in the mask. If the goal is to use short BDs for checksum on hardware that supports it, gate that on a capability check and update bnxt_start_xmit to match.
